newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds near static in becalmed summer market.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds near static in becalmed summer market.

text.p: Danish bond prices edged up marginally in a becalmed holiday market on Monday, with dealers seeing no activity of consequence ahead.

"Bonds have risen minimally despite the low turnover. We expect the whole week to be quiet due to the holidays. The only market moving data will be Tuesday's German June jobless figures and Friday's US PPI for the same month," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.06 point from the opening at 113.40, yielding 5.97 percent while the upcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark rose 0.08 point to 106.12, with the yield at 6.18 percent.
Turnover in the 2006 benchmark was around 550 million crowns, 320 million for the seven percent 2007 paper, which succeeds it on September 1.
The 2006 benchmark's August future rose 0.08 point to 112.62 with only one contract traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.15 point to 91.80.
The crown traded at 3.8073 per mark at 1045 GMT, virtually unchanged from the opening.
The 2007-bund 10-year yield gap was unaltered at 59 basis points.
